values: Student Template  |  Endicott College  |  Institutional Portfolio Management Project

This workbook has seven tabs: START HERE, SUMMARY, Client 1, Client 2, Client 3, ISSUER CHECK, and EVIDENCE LOG. Complete one client tab per assigned client, the required Issuer Reality Check rows, and one FactSet retrieval record for each recommendation and material portfolio-risk input.
Before You Start — Complete Phase 1 First

Your Phase 1 market view, client IPS, unresolved information gaps, and downstream guardrails must be approved before security research begins. Every candidate and Issuer Reality Check must trace to that mandate; the macro filter on each client tab must pass before selection.

Enter at least 10 securities per client (add rows as needed by copying an existing row). Weights in column G must sum to 100% — the total row turns green when correct. Column J (Macro Filter) must be YES for every holding. Link each security to a thesis number in column K.

Every client needs at least one derivative hedge (e.g. Protective Put). Document the chosen strategy in full — cost, strike, expiration, and net Bear Case impact. Then complete the alternative comparison table for at least one other strategy you considered and explain why you rejected it.

Complete one thesis block per security. Number must match column K in Section 1. Each block requires: macro connection, investment rationale, data citation, IPS suitability check, and an AI audit note if AI was used. Five blocks are pre-built; copy to add more.

Any AI tool used to suggest securities, expected returns, or hedge parameters must be documented in your team's AI Audit Log. The Hallucination Clause applies: unverified AI data = professional negligence. Every number must trace to FactSet, FRED, or SEC.

Reviewers will check: (1) weights sum to 100%, (2) macro filters pass, (3) each selected security has a completed thesis and candidate comparison, (4) every required direct or look-through exposure has an Issuer Reality Check, (5) yield or recent return is not the sole rationale, (6) sources and as-of dates are complete, and (7) the final mix satisfies the IPS and bear-case tripwire.

values: Required inside Security Analysis and Selection — not a separate accounting unit
DECISION RULE — Yield or recent return alone cannot support a recommendation. Evidence the issuer's financial health, operating outlook, and relevance to the client's mandate.
APPLIES TO — Every direct bond or equity exposure, plus the most material relevant issuer or holding within each selected mutual fund or ETF.

ROLE HANDOFF — Fixed-Income: credit review  |  Fund & ETF: look-through holdings/concentration  |  Client & Macro: scenario impact  |  Portfolio & Risk: allocation, diversification, stress, and monitoring

COMPLETION STANDARD — Concise and cited. Show consistent financial periods, label missing information, and end with a client-fit and allocation conclusion. A second team member reviews each row before committee approval.
BUS 331 — FactSet Research and Evidence Log
Required licensed-source record — document the retrieval, interpret the evidence, and explain its effect on the recommendation

BOUNDARY — Use licensed FactSet access for course research. Submit final work and required licensed-source evidence privately through Canvas. Do not place FactSet captures, exports, credentials, completed proprietary data files, or student work in the public repository.
NAVIGATION NOTE — FactSet layouts, labels, and entitlements can differ. Follow course demonstrations and current FactSet support; this log defines evidence requirements, not a click path.
